reasoning: Combined the two overlapping list-of-people proposals into one rule covering distinctive shared relations, including rulers’ common realms, while preserving the cautions against generic-role defaults and unsupported guesses. Kept the direct-definition guidance as a separate, nonredundant edit. Each edit is inserted after a distinct existing paragraph; no protected content is changed.

edits.target: When a prompt consists only of a list of character names or roles, use context to identify their shared work or program if that is the implied target. Return the work or program, not the performers, unless the prompt asks for the cast.
edits.content: For a prompt consisting only of several people’s names, use context to identify the distinctive shared relation the list is meant to cue (for example, a common country or realm for rulers), rather than defaulting to a generic common role. Return the shared entity or attribute the clue calls for, not a succession or family chain; do not guess when context leaves multiple relations equally plausible or establishes none.

edits.target: For compact definition or wordplay clues that give two linked readings, solve the whole clue for the conventional term satisfying both; do not merely restate one reading. Preserve an article when it is part of the expected expression.
edits.content: For direct definition or trivia clues, treat the description as a fill-in target and return the conventional term or category called for by the whole clue, including after elliptical wording such as “one of these.” Do not answer with a named example when the clue asks for its class, or repeat an embedded synonym that serves only as a cue rather than the target.
